The detector class is imported rather than reimplemented, and since `require_slope` and `breadth_key` are now real parameters, every structural variant in the table is the shipped code under a different configuration.

WHY NOT STRATEGY P&L. A backtest result mixes the label with the rule, the sizing and the fills and cannot say which one moved. What is scored here is only the detector's own claim: does the label order the forward return of the composite, and does it arrive in time.

THE SEARCH WAS IN A CAGE, AND HAD OPTIMISED DEEPER INTO IT. `trend_period` (100-300) and `confirmation_bars` (3-45) were already searchable, and after 84 iterations the incumbent held 284 and 43 -- an even SLOWER detector than the default. That is consistent: with the slope test mandatory, a faster detector produced a wrong BEAR label more often, so the search correctly fled toward inactivity. The `reachable-before` variant confirms the cage directly: built only from levers the loop already had, its BEAR forward return is still +0.81% and the falling fold still sits on the wrong side at +0.13%.

ABLATIONS. All three surviving changes carry weight and none explains the result alone. Reverting confirmation to 20 bars puts the falling fold back to +3.87%; reverting the trend window to 200 puts it at +3.27%; reverting breadth to sma_100 leaves it right (-4.82%) but breaks 2020-2022.

A COUPLING THAT WOULD HAVE MADE THE FIX INERT. `bear_min_age` gates bear-branch participation on bars elapsed in the current BEAR episode, and its default was 240. The old detector produced six BEAR episodes in eight years with a 324-bar maximum; the new one produces 24 with a 127-bar maximum, so NOT ONE BAR of the tape would have passed 240. The faster label would have arrived to find the gate it feeds welded shut. The default is now 30 -- about the first quartile of the new episode lengths, open for 588 of 1192 BEAR bars -- and the searchable range is 5-200 instead of 30-400.

HONEST LIMITS. 2022-2024 is the one fold where the adopted detector still points the wrong way (+1.57%); it is right in the other three, including -7.19% in 2024-2026, the fold the loop keeps losing. Three of the six falls are still never named -- 39.6% in 13 days, 26.5% in 4, 22.1% in 9. Two are inside warmup and the third is a flash crash; naming those is not what a MAJOR-trend detector is for. The reference basket is still six survivors, so the composite is still biased upward. And this is a detector measurement, not a P&L result: whether a better label earns money is what the loop now has to answer.
